candidate_sources.title: Postharvest Rots of Banana (PD-54)
candidate_sources.snippet: Publication PD-54 from October 2008 discusses anthracnose symptoms that occur as peel blemishes, as black or brown, sunken spots of various sizes on fruits that may bear masses of salmon-colored acervuli with their associated conidia. The pathogen survives readily on dead and dying plant tissues, including banana leaves, and spores are spread by splashing raindrop impact. Bunches should be sprayed with approved fungicides before bagging them with perforated polyethylene sleeves.

candidate_sources.title: Colletotrichum musae (tip rot of banana) - Plantwise Plus / CABI
candidate_sources.snippet: Colletotrichum musae is the fungus responsible for pre- and post-harvest banana anthracnose, the most important postharvest disease of banana, present in all production areas worldwide. On banana fruits the fungus causes sunken lesions which turn into sunken, dark patches with orange acervuli as the fruit ripens. Initial infection typically occurs during fruit development but remains latent until ripeness. Management includes covering emerging fruit with plastic, avoiding harvest damage, sanitation, and fungicide treatment.

candidate_sources.title: Characterisation of Colletotrichum Species Associated with Anthracnose of Banana
candidate_sources.snippet: Colletotrichum musae is the causal agent of anthracnose in banana fruits; infection by this fungal pathogen results in severe post-harvest losses. Symptoms include black and sunken lesions with spore masses or acervuli in the lesion. The fungus causes a latent (quiescent) infection in immature fruits, with symptoms gradually developing as the fruits ripen. Rapid spore germination and appressorium formation occur under high relative humidity and temperatures of 25-30 °C.

candidate_sources.title: Biology, pathology, and management of Colletotrichum musae and perspectives on developing anthracnose-resistant crop varieties
candidate_sources.snippet: Comprehensive review of biology, pathology, and management of Colletotrichum musae — causal agent of banana anthracnose/bitter rot. Covers infection process (spore germination, appressorium formation, latent infection), favorable conditions (25-30°C, high humidity), and management including resistant variety development.

candidate_sources.title: Banana Bunchy Top Virus
candidate_sources.snippet: University of Hawaii CTAHR extension publication PD-12 on Banana Bunchy Top Virus covering detailed symptoms, pathogen (BBTV), transmission by banana aphid Pentalonia nigronervosa, and management practices.

candidate_sources.snippet: Detailed signs and symptoms document from University of Hawaii CTAHR BBTD program describing dark green streaks on leaf midribs and petioles, 'Morse code' streaking, rosetted appearance, and stunted fruit in infected banana plants.

candidate_sources.title: Banana bunchy top virus (bunchy top of banana)
candidate_sources.snippet: CABI Plantwise Plus Knowledge Bank datasheet on Banana bunchy top virus covering identity, distribution, dispersal, hosts/species affected, vectors (banana aphid Pentalonia nigronervosa), diagnosis, biology, impacts, and prevention/control.

candidate_sources.snippet: ProMusa dedicated page on Bunchy top disease of banana describing the causal agent BBTV (genus Babuvirus, family Nanoviridae), symptoms, transmission by banana aphid, geographic distribution, and integrated management.

candidate_sources.title: Trachysphaera fructigena (cigar end rot of banana)
candidate_sources.snippet: CABI datasheet on Trachysphaera fructigena, the fungus causing cigar end rot of banana, including pathogen biology, symptoms, distribution, and management.

candidate_sources.title: Cigar end rot: Verticillium theobromae
candidate_sources.snippet: TNAU Agritech Portal factsheet describing cigar end rot of banana caused by Verticillium theobromae, including symptoms (blackening and folding of finger tips with corrugated ash-covered appearance) and management.

candidate_sources.title: Cigar end rot on banana - Plantwise Knowledge Bank
candidate_sources.snippet: Plantwise/CABI Pest Management Decision Guide for cigar end rot on banana covering symptoms, pathogen (Verticillium theobromae / Trachysphaera fructigena), favorable conditions, and recommended cultural and chemical management.

candidate_sources.title: Cigar end rot | Infonet Biovision
candidate_sources.snippet: Infonet Biovision page on cigar end rot of banana caused by Trachysphaera fructigena and Verticillium theobromae, describing the dry gray-to-black rot at the fruit tip covered in grayish fungal growth resembling cigar ash, and control measures.

candidate_sources.title: Cordana leaf spot | Improving the understanding of banana (ProMusa)
candidate_sources.snippet: Cordana leaf spot is a disease of banana that, even though it is common worldwide, has generally little impact on production. It is caused by two Neocordana fungi (Neocordana musae and Neocordana johnstonii), often found as secondary invaders of leaf lesions. Characteristic symptoms are large, pale brown, oval to fusiform necrotic lesions with pale grey concentric ring patterns, a dark brown border surrounded by a bright yellow halo.

candidate_sources.title: Cordana musae (Cordana leaf spot) | CABI Compendium
candidate_sources.snippet: CABI datasheet on Cordana musae covering Identity, Distribution, Hosts/Species Affected, Symptoms, Biology and Ecology, and Further Information. Neocordana musae (formerly Cordana musae) is an ascomycete fungus causing cordana leaf spot on bananas.

candidate_sources.title: Cordana leaf spot | Disease Treatment | Bayer Crop Science
candidate_sources.snippet: Yellow or pale brown, oval- or eye-shaped spots appear near the leaf margins of lower leaves. Over time, the spots enlarge and their central area becomes necrotic, forming a clear concentric zonation. Several spots can coalesce to form large necrotic patches surrounded by yellow tissues. Spores are produced in large quantities on the underside of leaves. Inoculum spreads through splashing water and wind.

candidate_sources.title: Banana diamond leaf spot (072) - Pacific Pests, Pathogens & Weeds (Lucid)
candidate_sources.snippet: Fact sheet covering banana diamond leaf spot / Cordana leaf spot caused by Neocordana musae, with symptoms, distribution, host range, impact, detection, management and cultural control for Pacific banana production.

candidate_sources.title: Chapter II: Key Pests and Pathogens of Banana in the Pacific — Fusarium Wilt or Panama Disease (University of Hawaii CTAHR)

candidate_sources.snippet: APS Phytopathology review article on Fusarium Wilt of Banana (Panama disease) caused by Fusarium oxysporum f. sp. cubense, covering pathogen races including TR4, symptoms, epidemiology, and management.

candidate_sources.snippet: Government extension Agnote covering Fusarium wilt / Panama disease of bananas: causal fungus Fusarium oxysporum f. sp. cubense, symptoms, spread, and on-farm management recommendations.

candidate_sources.title: First Report of Pestalotiopsis microspora Causing Leaf Blight of Banana in Bangladesh | Plant Disease
candidate_sources.snippet: First report documenting Pestalotiopsis microspora as a new pathogen causing leaf blight of banana in Bangladesh, with morphological and molecular identification of the pathogen and pathogenicity testing.

candidate_sources.title: BananaLSD: A banana leaf images dataset for classification of banana leaf diseases using machine learning - ScienceDirect
candidate_sources.snippet: Banana production faces serious challenges due to leaf spot diseases like Sigatoka, Cordana and Pestalotiopsis which reduce yield and increase production costs. Dataset includes annotated images of three prevalent diseased banana leaves: Pestalotiopsis, Sigatoka, and Cordana.

candidate_sources.title: PP-217/PP141: Pestalotiopsis (Pestalotia) Diseases of Palm
candidate_sources.snippet: UF/IFAS extension factsheet on Pestalotiopsis diseases. Spots begin as very small yellow, brown or black spots; spots may turn grayish and be outlined in black. The fungus usually requires wounds for plant penetration. Pestalotiopsis produces abundant spores that are easily dispersed by wind and water movement.

candidate_sources.title: BananaLSD: A banana leaf images dataset for classification of banana leaf diseases using machine learning - PMC
candidate_sources.snippet: PMC-hosted open-access version describing Pestalotiopsis leaf spot alongside Sigatoka and Cordana as three prevalent banana leaf diseases, with symptom descriptions and image annotations used for disease identification.

candidate_sources.title: Phaeoseptoria musae - Wikipedia
candidate_sources.snippet: Phaeoseptoria musae is a plant pathogen infecting banana and plantain. Phaeoseptoria musae is the cause of Phaeoseptoria leaf spot, which produces symptoms very similar to Sigatoka. Visible symptoms on mature leaves are elliptical lesions 1-2 cm wide, straw yellow in the centre with dark brown margins and yellow haloes. As the disease progresses the spots enlarge, coalesce producing large irregular necrotic lesions with whitish to straw centres.

candidate_sources.title: Phaeoseptoria Leaf Spot (Phaeoseptoria musae Punith., 1977)
candidate_sources.snippet: Phaeoseptoria Leaf Spot caused by Phaeoseptoria musae Punith., 1977. Dedicated subject page providing taxonomic information, images and distribution for the banana Phaeoseptoria leaf spot pathogen. Hosted by the Center for Invasive Species and Ecosystem Health at the University of Georgia in cooperation with USDA.

candidate_sources.title: List of banana and plantain diseases - Wikipedia
candidate_sources.snippet: Comprehensive list of banana and plantain diseases including Phaeoseptoria leaf spot caused by Phaeoseptoria musae, alongside Sigatoka, black leaf streak, Cordana leaf spot, and other foliar diseases of Musa spp. Provides pathogen names and brief disease descriptions.

candidate_sources.title: Diseases of quarantine and economic importance in banana tree (Musa sp.) in México
candidate_sources.snippet: Peer-reviewed review of banana diseases of quarantine and economic importance, including Phaeoseptoria leaf spot (Phaeoseptoria musae). Describes symptoms as small necrotic, lentis-shaped dark brown spots similar to Sigatoka, which enlarge rapidly; discusses distribution and control.

candidate_sources.title: Leaf Blotch of Banana | Pests & Diseases
candidate_sources.snippet: Phoma-related leaf disease on banana showing symptoms progressing from reddish brown spots to ovoid-shaped lesions, eventually becoming necrotic, dry and gray with a yellow halo. Early stages show small, circular, pale brown spots that expand with concentric rings. Infected leaf tissue contains blackish pycnidia releasing conidia in humid conditions.

candidate_sources.title: Phoma herbarum (brown leaf spot and stem canker) | CABI Compendium
candidate_sources.snippet: CABI datasheet on Phoma herbarum covering brown leaf spot and stem canker — identity, distribution, hosts/species affected, symptoms, biology, and management of Phoma blight-related pathogens.

candidate_sources.title: Banana Diseases and Pests Field Guide for Diagnostics and Data Collection (IITA/Bioversity)
candidate_sources.snippet: Comprehensive field guide produced by IITA/Bioversity for diagnostics and data collection of banana diseases and pests, including fungal leaf spot diseases affecting Musa spp. Covers symptom recognition, pathogen identification, and field management of minor and major banana diseases.

candidate_sources.title: Molecular Identification of Endophytic Fungi from Banana Leaves (Musa spp.)
candidate_sources.snippet: Peer-reviewed study identifying Phoma sorghina as an endophytic/associated fungal species isolated from banana leaves (Musa spp.), providing molecular identification and context for Phoma species occurring on banana foliage.

candidate_sources.title: Guignardia musae (freckle disease of banana) | CABI Compendium
candidate_sources.snippet: CABI Compendium datasheet on Guignardia musae (anamorph Phyllosticta musarum), the causal agent of freckle disease / Phyllosticta leaf spot of banana, with detailed information on pathogen biology, symptoms, distribution and control.

candidate_sources.title: Fact sheet - Banana freckle (124) - Pacific Pests, Pathogens and Weeds
candidate_sources.snippet: Pacific Pests, Pathogens and Weeds factsheet on banana freckle caused by Phyllosticta musarum / Guignardia musae. Describes symptoms (small dark brown freckles with sandpapery feel on leaves and fruit), source of infection, spread, host range and cultural and chemical management.

candidate_sources.title: Banana freckle | Business Queensland
candidate_sources.snippet: Queensland Government biosecurity factsheet on banana freckle (Phyllosticta cavendishii / P. musarum): description of leaf and fruit symptoms as small, raised dark spots with a sandpapery texture, host range, disease cycle, spread, and management / reporting requirements.

candidate_sources.title: Phyllosticta species associated with freckle disease of banana | Fungal Diversity
candidate_sources.snippet: Peer-reviewed taxonomic study in Fungal Diversity characterizing the Phyllosticta species complex causing freckle/leaf spot disease of banana, including Phyllosticta maculata, P. musarum, P. cavendishii and P. capitalensis, with morphological and molecular data from a global specimen set.

candidate_sources.title: Mycosphaerella fijiensis (black Sigatoka) | CABI Compendium
candidate_sources.snippet: The CABI Compendium datasheet on Mycosphaerella fijiensis covers Identity, Overview, Distribution, Dispersal, Hosts/Species Affected, Diagnosis, Biology & Ecology, Impacts, Prevention/Control, and Further Information. The asexual name is Paracercospora fijiensis (previously Pseudocercospora fijiensis).

candidate_sources.title: Key Pests and Pathogens of Banana | Black Leaf Streak or Sigatoka Disease — CTAHR, University of Hawaii
candidate_sources.snippet: Chapter II of the CTAHR Banana IPM Guidebook covering Black Leaf Streak / Sigatoka Disease caused by Pseudocercospora fijiensis, including symptomatology, pathogen biology, and integrated management options for banana growers.

candidate_sources.title: Overview of the Sigatoka leaf spot complex in banana and its current management
candidate_sources.snippet: The Sigatoka leaf spot complex includes three major pathogens: Pseudocercospora musae (yellow Sigatoka), P. eumusae (eumusae leaf spot disease), and P. fijiensis (black Sigatoka). Symptoms progress from yellow/brown streaks to elliptic necrotic spots parallel to secondary veins; management combines cultural practices, resistant cultivars, and fungicides.
